Since \(y>0\),
\[
\frac{y}{\sqrt{1+y^2}} = \cos\left(\arctan \frac1y\right),
\]
so
\[
\arccos \frac{y}{\sqrt{1+y^2}}=\arctan \frac1y.
\]
Also,
\[
\arcsin \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}=\arctan 3
\]
because \(\sin \theta=\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\) and \(\cos \theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\), so \(\tan \theta=3\).

Thus the equation becomes
\[
\arctan x+\arctan \frac1y=\arctan 3.
\]
Taking tangent of both sides,
\[
\frac{x+\frac1y}{1-\frac{x}{y}}=3.
\]
Multiply by \(y\):
\[
xy+1=3y-3x.
\]
So
\[
xy+3x-3y+1=0.
\]
Therefore,
\[
(a,b,c)=(3,-3,1).
\]

The answer is \((3,-3,1)\).
